title: Decode: MegaMoE NVFP4 EP32 + shared-expert overlap
shape: D3-32 r24 1-node slice (EP4 emulating EP32: 28 active experts/rank split 14+14 over the die halves, EP32 MegaMoE records via knob_world_size; SP shard 96 MoE tokens/GPU, top-16, L~135K, k=3); ms = 23-layer slice x4 (92 MoE layers)
basis: MEASURED in-step, NVFP4 checkpoint, L24 1-node D3-32 slice at r24 (die-split emulation, EP32 records), MegaMoE family exposed per 23 layers (ms): baseline int 9d3cb2b0c2 = 1.786 (runs/INFRA/step_d/ref9d3-ds-nv-prof), current int c8a403aa7f (D-MOE 4b58015c31 merged) = 1.599 (t7-ds-nv-prof); achievable = fused nvfp4_modelopt MegaMoE row L24 r24 0.85 (INFRA 17:50 model fix; was 1.316 additive). Real EP32 (8 nodes, 93 layers, int 5718ef2): exposed 6.55 vs fused ach 3.40 ms.
gap_analysis: Real EP32 r24 in-step per layer (d8-int5718ef2 traces, 32 ranks): stage 3.0 us -> MegaMoE router kernel 15.5 us (size exchange + metadata push over 31 peers + rank skew; main kernel PDL-resident at +0.8) -> main kernel ends +80 (min/med/max over ranks 73/80/86 us: ~12 us arrival skew) -> separate reduce 4.2 -> latent rms_norm 2.6 -> latent_up. Shared expert on the side stream: gate_up runs beside the router (-1..10 us), act_quant 10.5-20 us (9.7 us, starved by the full MegaMoE grid), shared down cannot get SMs until MegaMoE ends (74-85 us) and finishes ~4 us after the main kernel: it becomes critical once the reduce/norm shrink. SOL per layer at r24 ~ max(520 MB die-local stream 30 us, NVLink combine ~10 us) + 2 dependent NVLink rounds ~6 us = fused model 36.6 us. Gap to close ~33 us/layer: (1) front: router 15.5 us at EP32 (1-node 3.4) -> single-round size publication (multimem) + weight prefetch into L2 during the wait (E1, 126 MB L2 = ~5 us of stream); (2) tail: reduce 4.2 + norm 2.6 -> one fused kernel (E2a, in test) then into the kernel tail (E2b); (3) shared expert: run it in the router-wait window or on a fixed SM budget so it neither starves MegaMoE nor trails it; (4) main kernel after sizes 60-65 us vs 1-GPU 40: needs the real-EP32 stamps (queued 8n) to split comm vs stream vs imbalance.
inefficiencies: FIXED on the branch: D3-32 decode used DeepGEMM fp8_fp4 MegaMoE (149 us/layer exposed at r24 in the slice); kimi_k3_mega_moe on the re-vendored kernel: 68 us/layer exposed
MEASURED (stamps, 1 GPU T96): weights stream only after the router publishes sizes (~3 us after the call starts); at T>=4 every local expert is active so the weight stream does not depend on routing
MEASURED: CTA finish imbalance ~4 us at the end of the stream (median vs max last-MMA end), then a ~1.2 us tail barrier
MEASURED: separate BF16 top-k reduce kernel ~2.7 us and NVFP4 quant/stage kernel ~1.9 us per call around the persistent kernel
MEASURED (Hecate EP32 vs 1 GPU): ~17 us/call of dispatch/combine latency not hidden behind the weight stream at EP32
MEASURED: stream phase itself ~85-90% of the die-local HBM rate (weights die-localized + die_split active)
In-tree D3-32 runs vendored DeepGEMM fp8_fp4 (no NVFP4 EP32 backend); shared experts serial on that path (fix: megamoe_rubin re-vendor, landed on the branch)
rubin_features: NVFP4 block-scaled tcgen05 MMA (E4M3 block-16 scales)
NVLink symmetric memory one-sided dispatch/combine (multimem where applicable)
Mixed CGA clusters (4x1 / 2x1) and TMA multicast
L2 persistence hints for the decode weight stream
PDL (programmatic dependent launch) to overlap the MegaMoE prologue with the router GEMM
plan: RUNNING 8n real-EP32 standalone (runs/D-MOE/vs8.sh plan: plain T4-128, stamped T4-96, E1 0/40 MiB) -> per-phase split at real EP32
IN TEST E2a fused reduce+latent RMSNorm (wzhao/k31ws-d-moe 728a82c351, merged int 0289388c5b): unit test + slice A/B vs int trial9-4071a79-1
E2b reduce+norm into the main kernel tail (after the NVLink barrier with an epilogue grid sync)
E4 router: one-round size publication (multimem.st.async.release) + E1 L2 weight prefetch during the size wait, judged at real EP32
E5 shared expert placement: run in the router-wait window / SM-budgeted beside MegaMoE; in-step A/B on the 8n hold (1-node front is too short to judge)
